terms.meaning: The list of names a package officially makes available to other code.
A separate file inside a package. Here, each kind of record has its own file.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Imports from the assessment and assumption modules
sections.what: Brings in the judgement types, the assumption types, the confidence types, and the current-state types from their own files. These are the first group of names the package makes available.
sections.why: Likely reason: to give callers one place to import from. The code does not say this directly, but the module docstring does.
sections.watch_out: A type added to a submodule does nothing for callers until it is also imported here.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Imports from the enum, feasibility and reconciliation modules
sections.what: Brings in the closed word lists, the feasibility types, the future-state types, the run manifest types, and the matching and reconciliation types. Part of the public export list also starts here.
sections.why: Same reason as the earlier imports: one import point for all callers. The reason for splitting by file is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The export list controls what a star import brings in, and nothing checks that it matches the import list above.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Export list for the whole package
sections.what: Finishes the public export list, naming the remaining types and constants, including the record types and the shared range types. This list defines what the package publicly promises.
sections.why: Likely reason: to make the public surface explicit, so internal names stay internal. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: Nothing checks that every imported name appears here, so a new public type can be left out without any error.

summary: The single import point for the process schema package. It gathers the data definitions from its submodules and lists the names it officially makes available.
purpose: Lets the rest of the project import every schema type from one place, without knowing which internal file defines it.
why: The module docstring says internal reorganisation must not break callers, so consumers import from here. Likely reason for the explicit export list: to say which names are public. This is not stated in the code.
how: Imports each named type and constant from its submodule, then lists the public names in an export list. The docstring asks the reader to read the package's guide file and request a schema-guardian review before changing anything in the package.
inputs: No runtime input. It reads the submodules of the schema package when it is loaded.
outputs: The named types and constants that other code can import from the schema package.
risks: Adding a type to its submodule but forgetting to add it here, or changing a name here, which breaks every importer. The import list and the export list are kept by hand, and nothing in this file checks that they match.
debug: If an import fails with a missing name, check that the name is in both the import list and the export list here. Then check that the submodule defining it loads without errors.
